newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire tax revenues to exceed expectations.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire tax revenues to exceed expectations.

text.p: House Finance Committee officials said late Wednesday they were elated that revenue from New Hampshire taxes will increase an unexpected $62.9 million over the next two years.
The state's two biggest moneymakers, the Business Profits and Business Enterprise taxes, came in some $12 million more than expected last month and are running far above earlier projections.

Department of Revenue Administration Commissioner Stan Arnold told House budget writers that the Business Profits tax generated more than $112 million as of March 31, about 23 percent ahead of legislative projections.
The Business Enterprise tax brought in $5.1 million more than lawmakers had projected, Arnold said.
Other taxes posting better than expected revenues include the real estate transfer tax, the telecommunications tax and the tobacco tax.

The news prompted House Finance Committee chairman Neal Kurk (R-Weare) to predict that a projected $37 million budget deficit will be smaller than expected. Kurk also said the news gives budget writers some relief as they weigh a kindergarten expansion and other programs.

But the revenue news was not all good. House Finance Committee officials said they are bracing for word concerning millions of dollars in federal Medicaid reimbursement funds from a tax on hospitals. The state has used the funds for nearly a decade to balance its biennial budget.
Congress has reduced funding for the program. The state budget is expected to be voted on in the House next week.
